situation:
You are the senior manager of content operations and the manager of subscriber engagement at BEACONSTREAM, a streaming platform built around a founder-curated slate of original films and documentaries. The vice president of product experience (judge) has called you in together. BEACONSTREAM has built its reputation on editorial trust, but a newer entrant, NOVAWAVE, has pulled ahead in weekly active users this quarter using a recommendation engine that resurfaces older titles every night. The vice president wants a recommendation before the next board update.

The data engineer who built BEACONSTREAM's original recommendation model has requested a modified schedule under a documented medical condition, shifting to remote afternoons and away from the overnight on-call rotation that currently supports late-night model retraining. That retraining window is the only place engineers can safely test changes before the personalization overhaul ships. The overhaul is BEACONSTREAM's answer to NOVAWAVE's growth, and subscriber engagement has already promised subscribers a faster, more relevant homepage within six weeks.

One option keeps the retraining rotation staffed by asking a contractor to shadow the overnight runs for the length of the accommodation, freeing the recommendation model to finish on schedule and letting the overhaul launch in time to compete with NOVAWAVE before subscribers renew for the season. The contractor has never touched BEACONSTREAM's recommendation code, learns it under deadline pressure, and rolls off once the accommodation period ends, leaving no one who has carried the testing work past this quarter.

The alternative honors the accommodation exactly as requested, moving the retraining window to daytime hours the engineer can cover and pushing the launch date back several weeks. Subscriber engagement's promotional plan for the overhaul, already built around this season's premieres, would need to shift instead to a quieter push merchandising BEACONSTREAM's existing library, at the very moment NOVAWAVE is spending most heavily to win over BEACONSTREAM's subscribers.

The vice president wants the participant team's recommendation on how to handle the accommodation request without slowing the personalization launch beyond what the business can absorb, and on how that decision should be communicated to the data engineer, to the rest of the engineering team, and to subscriber engagement's promotional planning, so that everyone is working from the same understanding of what changed, and why it changed.

The vice president of product experience (judge) will greet the participant team, ask to hear their recommendation, and listen for how they propose enlisting the engineering team and subscriber engagement around whichever plan they choose. After the presentation and the judge's questions, the vice president will thank the participant team for their work and close the meeting.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president of product experience at BEACONSTREAM. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the participant team to recommend how to handle the data engineer's accommodation request without letting the personalization overhaul fall further behind NOVAWAVE, and to recommend how that decision should be communicated to the data engineer, to the rest of the engineering team, and to subscriber engagement's promotional planning.

During the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Why does the timing of this accommodation matter to the launch, and to whom does that timing matter most?
Why would the way this decision is communicated change how the data engineer and the rest of the engineering team respond to it?
